question: Should Telegram expose standalone `pin` and `unpin` message-tool actions, and what gate plus target semantics should protect them?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but exposing these actions gives agents persistent chat-state mutation power through privileged bot credentials, and current config has no pin-specific gate or approved implicit-unpin contract.

options.title: Approve gated explicit actions
options.body: Add Telegram-plugin-owned `pin` and `unpin` actions behind an explicit per-account action gate, require a concrete `messageId` unless separately approved, and require live Telegram proof before merge.

options.title: Keep delivery pin only
options.body: Do not expose standalone pin/unpin actions yet; keep the existing `delivery.pin` support limited to messages OpenClaw just sent.

options.title: Request design first
options.body: Ask for a short design note covering admin-right expectations, per-account gating, implicit unpin behavior, and forum-topic semantics before implementation.

recommendation.title: Approve gated explicit actions
recommendation.body: Add Telegram-plugin-owned `pin` and `unpin` actions behind an explicit per-account action gate, require a concrete `messageId` unless separately approved, and require live Telegram proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The likely decision should route to the contributor who consolidated Telegram message-tool discovery and moved the action runtime seam this feature would extend.
